data.title: WHO Diagnostic Criteria and Classification of Hyperglycaemia First Detected in Pregnancy and Diabetes
data.text: WHO defines diabetes mellitus as fasting plasma glucose >= 7.0 mmol/L (126 mg/dL) or 2-hour post-load plasma glucose >= 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL), or HbA1c >= 6.5% (48 mmol/mol). Diagnosis requires a second confirmatory test in the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia with acute metabolic decompensation.

data.title: WHO Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Hypertension in Adults
data.text: WHO recommends initiating pharmacological antihypertensive treatment in individuals with a confirmed diagnosis of hypertension of systolic blood pressure >= 140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure >= 90 mmHg. For low blood pressure, a reading below 90/60 mmHg is generally defined as hypotension, but requires assessment of symptoms (dizziness, fainting) and volume status before diagnosing pathological hypotension.
